Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 10291 of 2023
Applicant :- Deepak
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. Lko And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- S.C. Misra,Arun Kumar Gupta,Indresh Kumar Mishra Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. No one appears on behalf of the respondent no.2 despite service of notice.

3. In terms of the F.I.R., it was alleged that on 21.3.2023 at about 5.30 p.m., three accused including the applicant had caught hold of the hand of the daughter of the informant with malafide intention,
however when she raised hue and cry, all the accused ran away.
In the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the similar allegations were levelled.
Subsequently, in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., however she stated that on the said date, the applicant had committed rape on her which span over 56 minutes.
The allegations were levelled that on 21.3.2023 at about 5.30 p.m. the offence was committed.
The medical on record does not corroborate the allegation levelled under Section Deepak vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ...

P.C. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the medical on record indicates the age of the victim as 15 years.

4. Learned A.G.A. points out that the age of the victim as per the transfer certificate of Class VIII is around 14 years, however none of the said documents are enough to conclusively determine the age of the victim at this stage in terms of the procedure prescribed under Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice Act and the rules framed thereunder to form a view with regard to age determination of the victim, as such the same would be decided at the time of trial in view of the law laid down in the case of Monish Vs. State of U.P. passed by this Court in Crl. Misc. Bail Application No.55026 of 2021 decided on 9.2.2023.

entities.text: Crl. Misc. Bail Application No.55026 of 2021
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The applicant is languishing in jail since 27.3.2023 and has no criminal antecedents, hence the applicant may be released on bail.
5. Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail.

6. Considering the fact that the allegations of offence under Section 376 I.P.C. were levelled only in the statement of the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C., which too are not corroborated by the medical on record and there is no conclusive document to form a view with regard to the age of the prosecutrix, and the age of the victim is to be determined at the time of the trial in view of the law laid down in the case of Monish Vs. State of U.P.(supra) as well as in terms of the Juvenile Justice Act and the rules framed thereunder; the applicant is in jail since 27.3.2023 and has no criminal antecedents, and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail,
would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
7.
Accordingly, the application for grant of bail is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Deepak be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.109 of 2023, under Sections 376-D, 323, 506 I.P.C. and Section 5(Chha)/6 of the POCSO Act, Police Station Madhoganj, District Hardoi on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 15.2.2024/
